parts.str: Survey about your health status in the last week.
this will take 15 seconds to 3 minutes to complete, depending on your symptoms

NOTE 1: If you are filling this in on behalf of someone else, please answer all the questions as if you are that person

NOTE 2: Please remember that any information you report in FluSurvey on use of Flu or COVID-19 tests is not shared with your GP or other healthcare provider. Please contact them directly if you wish for them to be aware of your test results.

Please update your profile survey for this season so that we have the latest data for monitoring respiratory viruses in your community: [Update your FluSurvey profile survey](https://flusurvey.net/survey/flusurvey/intake).
Have you had any of the following symptoms in the past week?
Diarrhoea (at least three times a day)

**Why are we asking this?**  

The key part of this survey is tracking respiratory symptoms in the community.  

**How should I answer it?**  

For people with chronic (long-term) illnesses, only tick changes in symptoms. For example, if you have chronic shortness of breath then only tick this box if this has got worse recently.
Please select all options that apply.
Because of your symptoms, did you use testing at home or were you tested in any health services in relation to these symptoms?
No, I have not been tested
Yes, I tested positive for COVID-19
Yes, I tested positive for Flu
Yes, I tested positive for RSV
Yes, I tested positive for more than one of COVID-19, Flu or RSV
Yes, I tested positive for another infection
Yes, I was tested but the result was negative

**Why are we asking this?**  
Respiratory infections can present with similar symptoms. It is helpful to understand what may be causing your symptoms. 

**How should I answer it?** 

If you were tested and the result was negative, please select “Yes, I was tested but the result was negative”. If your test result was positive, please select the relevant option depending on your result. If you were not tested, please select “No, I have not been tested”.
On date of last visit, you reported that you were still ill with symptoms. Are the symptoms you reported today part of the same bout of illness?

**Why are we asking this?**

To make filling out the rest of the survey quicker for you.

**How should I answer it?**

If you believe that the symptoms you have reported today are caused by the same bout of illness as your previous symptoms, please tick “yes”.
When did the first symptoms appear?

**Why are we asking this?**

To help us work out the number of cases that arise each day.

**How should I answer it?**

Please give as accurate an estimate as possible.

**Why are we asking this?**

Using the beginning and end dates of symptoms we can work out how long respiratory infections last.

**How should I answer it?**

Please give as accurate an estimate as possible.
Did your symptoms develop suddenly over a few hours?

**Why are we asking this?**

Sudden onset of symptoms is believed to be common for flu.

**How should I answer it?**

Tick yes if your symptoms appeared over a few hours rather than gradually developing over a few days.

**Why are we asking this?**

Fever is very important for diagnosing flu, so we want to know when this started.

**How should I answer it?**

Please give as accurate an estimate as possible.

**Why are we asking this?**

Infections often cause a high temperature. However, not everyone takes their temperature when they are ill.

**How should I answer it?**

Answer yes, if you took your temperature using a thermometer.
What was your highest temperature measured?

**Why are we asking this?**

Certain infections often cause a high temperature.

**How should I answer it?**

Give the highest temperature you recorded during this episode of illness.
Because of your symptoms, did you VISIT (see face to face) any medical services?

**Why are we asking this?**

To find out whether people contact the health services because of their symptoms.

**How should I answer it?**

Tick all of those that apply. If you are due to attend, then tick the final option.
GP or another health professional at your GP practice
Hospital accident & emergency department / out of hours service
No, but I have an appointment scheduled
How soon after your symptoms appeared did you first VISIT a medical service?

**Why are we asking this?**

To find out how quickly people with symptoms are seen by the health services.

**How should I answer it?**

Only record the time until your FIRST contact with the health services.
Select the correct number of days
GP or another health professional at your GP practice
Hospital accident & department/out of hours service
Because of your symptoms, did you contact via TELEPHONE or INTERNET any medical services?

**Why are we asking this?**

To find out whether people contact the health services because of their symptoms.

**How should I answer it?**

Tick all of those that apply. If you are due to attend, then tick the final option.
GP or another health professional at your GP practice
No, but I have an appointment scheduled
How soon after your symptoms appeared did you first contact a medical service via TELEPHONE or INTERNET?

**Why are we asking this?**

To find out how quickly people with symptoms are seen by the health services.

**How should I answer it?**

Only record the time until your FIRST contact with the health services.
Select the correct number of days
GP or another health professional at your GP practice
Did you take medication for these symptoms?

**Why are we asking this?**

To find out who gets treated, and how effective treatment is.

**How should I answer it?**

Only record those medications that you used because of this illness. If you are on other medications because of a pre-existing illness then do not record these.
Pain killers (e.g. paracetamol including Lemsip and Calpol, ibuprofen, aspirin, etc)
COVID-19 medical treatments such as Paxlovid or sotrovimab
Other alternative medicine (essential oil, physiotherapy, etc.)
How long after the beginning of your symptoms did you start taking antiviral medication?

**Why are we asking this?**

Antivirals are thought to be most effective if taken quickly after disease onset.

**How should I answer it?**

Report the time until you first started taking antivirals (which may not be the same day as you got your prescription).
Did you change your daily routine because of your illness?

**Why are we asking this?**
We would like to understand the impact of your symptoms on your daily routine.
Did you take time off work/school because of your illness?
Not applicable (I am not employed or in education)

**Why are we asking this?**
We would like to understand the impact of your symptoms on your daily routine.


**How should I answer it?**
Tick "yes" if you would be at work/school today if you were not currently ill. If you are not employed or in education, please select "Not applicable".
How long have you been off work/school? (include number of days up to today, if you are still off work/ school)

**Why are we asking this?**

To measure the effect of symptoms on people’s daily lives.

**How should I answer it?**

Only count the days that you normally would have been in school or work (e.g. don’t count weekends).
Over the course of yesterday, how many people (outside your household) did you approach at a distance lower than 1 metre?

**Why are we asking this?**   
Respiratory infections can spread via social contacts. Measuring how we meet each other helps understand and predict outbreaks and transmission. 
**How should I answer it?** 
Try to think how many people you came across yesterday as best you can.
On a scale from 0 (bad) to 100 (perfect), how  was your health last week?
The scale goes from 0 to 100, 100 means the best health status you can imagine and 0 means the worst health status you can imagine.
Change the value of the slider by dragging the button.

## Infos about swabbing

Eligible are:

* 18 years old
* currently lives in England 

We have limited number lab capacity available per week. If you are interested and eligible, we will send you an email shortly with further information.

## Information on self-swabbing

To support our public health surveillance, UKHSA are offering eligible participants with specific symptoms the chance for a free postal respiratory swab test for a range of respiratory viruses. This respiratory swab test involves taking a sample from the back of your throat and from the inside of your nose. 

*Please note that currently self-swabbing is only open to participants over 18 years old and who live in England.*  

If you are reporting symptoms on behalf of someone else in your household, please answer these based on their details, and make sure to check that they are willing to participate.
I am interested in more information on this self-swabbing study
Yes, I want to do the swabbing this week

If you agree, UKHSA will contact you by email with a link to a partner website ([TakeATestUK](https://takeatestuk.com/)) to provide additional information. Your information will be handled securely by Take a Test UK and limited information will be shared with UKHSA to enable us to identify your sample and test results. 

Please note that by agreeing to participate in self-swabbing, you understand that: 

* Your test results will be held securely by UKHSA and can be linked back to your survey data 
* You will receive certain test results (such as flu and COVID-19) but this test is not intended as a clinical diagnosis or to inform your treatment. If you need urgent results for your individual care, you should not use this service. 
* To help us understand risk factors and outcomes of respiratory viruses, your test results will be linked to securely held health data at UKHSA, such as previous immunisations and administrative health records    
* These test results will only be sent to you and not to your GP 
* You can find full details about how your data will be used, stored, and protected - including the process of withdrawing from the study - in [our Privacy notice](https://flusurvey.net/legal/privacy-postal-swabbing)
I have reviewed and the information provided, including the privacy notice, and agree to take part in this self-swabbing study
If you agree, you will receive an email containing your free swab test request code in approximately 30 minutes.
If you have not received your free swab test request code in 30 minutes please contact us at [flusurvey.swab@ukhsa.gov.uk](mailto:flusurvey.swab@ukhsa.gov.uk)
Thank you for your filling out the questionnaire. Click submit to send in the responses.
